title: Advanced Dataset Operations 🧬
description: Master interleave, flat_map, window, zip, and handling multiple files.

slides.title: Beyond the Basics 🧰
slides.content:
# When Simple Shuffle/Batch Isn't Enough

- **Interleave**: read from many files in parallel, mixing records.
- **Flat_map**: map each element to a dataset and flatten.
- **Window**: group elements into fixed‑size windows for time series.
- **Zip**: combine multiple datasets element‑wise.
- **Concatenate**: append one dataset to another.

slides.title: Interleave for File Reading
slides.codeSnippet:
files = tf.data.Dataset.list_files('data/train/*.tfrecord')
dataset = files.interleave(
    tf.data.TFRecordDataset,
    cycle_length=4,          # how many files to read in parallel
    num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE
)

quizData.question: What does `cycle_length` control in `interleave`?

options.text: The number of output elements per input file
The number of input elements to interleave concurrently

quizData.explanation: `cycle_length` determines how many files (or datasets) are processed in parallel at a time.

slides.title: Flat_map for Tokenisation 🪙
slides.content:
# Flatten Nested Sequences

When each file contains multiple records and you want to output records one by one:

```python
def parse_file(filename):
    return tf.data.TextLineDataset(filename)

files = tf.data.Dataset.list_files('data/*.txt')
lines = files.flat_map(parse_file)
```
Each file yields lines; `flat_map` concatenates all lines into a single dataset.

slides.title: Windowing for Time Series 🪟
slides.content: Create sliding windows of data points.
slides.codeSnippet:
data = tf.data.Dataset.range(100)
windows = data.window(size=10, shift=5, drop_remainder=True)
# Each window is itself a dataset; use flat_map to process
windows = windows.flat_map(lambda w: w.batch(10))
# Now each element is a tensor of shape (10,)

slides.title: Zip & Concatenate
slides.codeSnippet:
# Zip: pair features and labels from separate sources
features = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices([...])
labels = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices([...])
dataset = tf.data.Dataset.zip((features, labels))

# Concatenate
dataset = dataset_A.concatenate(dataset_B)

slides.title: Use Interleave for Scalability 📈
slides.content: When you have thousands of files, interleave with a high `cycle_length` and `num_parallel_calls` can keep I/O busy, drastically reducing training time.
